5UPR Yards by Captain Yard

Five yards. Ninety days. Then we do it again.

Captain Yard has been in the market and running. What we kept finding is that the yards using it were still losing work upstream of the software — at the counter, in the quote pile, in accounts that quietly stopped calling. So we built a service around the engine to close that gap, and we run it five yards at a time.

Take a seat ↗
Why five

It is a capacity number, not a marketing device.

Our people answer your phone using your name. That is not something anybody does for forty yards at once and still does well. Five is what we can carry properly through a ninety-day cycle, so five is what we take.

Named closers

The same people on your account for the whole ninety days. Not a pool, not a rota, not whoever is free.

Ninety days, then out

A cycle ends, the system stays, and the seat frees up for the next cohort. That is what makes five sustainable.

One yard per market

Our closers cannot ring the same contractor on Tuesday for you and Thursday for the yard two exits down.

Full is full

When the fifth seat goes we say so, and we do not quietly take a sixth because somebody asked nicely.

The Founding Yard Charter

What Cohort 01 gets that Cohort 04 will not.

Not a discount. Discounting a service delivered by people is just a promise to care less, and you would feel it by week three. These are terms instead — things that cost us something real and are worth more to you than money off.

Activation waived

01

Setup, the fleet build, the rate cards, the scripts and the integration work. Founding yards pay for the ninety days of desk, not for the week that gets them live.

Worth a full activation

Your rate, locked for life

02

Cohort 01's monthly rate is the rate you keep for as long as you stay, through every future increase. When the published price moves — and it moves when a cohort fills — it does not move for anybody already inside.

Forever, in the agreement

Your metro, closed

03

One yard per market, per category, for as long as you stay. We turn away your competitors while you hold the seat. This one is a real cost to us, which is exactly why it is worth having.

Exclusivity, in writing

The Founding Exit

04

No ninety-day lock. Leave in month two if we are not earning it, and keep everything already built: the quoting system on your site, your fleet data, rate cards, pricing rules and every script. We would rather you could leave and choose not to.

No lock-in, ever

A seat on the roadmap

05

Founding yards get a standing call with the people who build Captain Yard. What breaks at your counter gets fixed for everybody, and you get to say what the engine learns to do next.

Direct line

The second yard, same rate

06

If you run more than one location, the second comes in at your founding rate whenever you are ready for it — not at whatever the price has become by then.

Extends to your group
What we ask back

It is a trade, and we would rather write it down than imply it.

Founding terms exist because the first five yards are worth more to us than money. They are what turns an argument into evidence. Here is exactly what we want in return, and none of it is a surprise on day sixty.

The trade, in full
  • Permission to publish your ninety-day numbers
  • Your name and logo on the case study
  • One reference call a quarter with a yard like yours
  • Twenty minutes of your own time, weekly
  • Honest feedback when something is not working

Publication is on your approval, line by line. If the numbers are ugly you can still say no, and the rest of the Charter does not change.

The four things that make this fail

We say them on the call, not in the small print.

Fleet data inside five days. Script approvals inside two. Your estimator turning quotes around in a business day. You personally on the weekly twenty minutes. Every engagement that has struggled has struggled on one of those four, and none of them are things we can do for you.

See what we actually run ↗
If the cohort is full

You do not sit in a queue for ninety days.

Deploy Captain Yard now — the full rent-it-out system on your own website, quoting, live availability, booking — and your seat in the next cohort is booked the day it opens. You start catching inquiries this week instead of next quarter, and when the closers arrive your fleet is already built, so the ninety days starts at full speed rather than in setup.

It is the better path for most yards anyway. Get the machine working before you add people on top of it.
